keyFindings: Cushioning: NITROFOAM feels relatively soft with good impact protection in the 38 mm heel, but the 30 mm forefoot rides firmer because the stiff plate dominates forefoot feel.

Responsiveness: Energy return is high (described as very responsive with noticeable bounce), especially at tempo/faster paces, though snappy rocker/plate behavior is highly mechanics-dependent and can feel like fighting the shoe.

Stability: Forefoot rigidity is very high from the carbon-composite plate, while the midfoot is more compliant; heel hold is secure via a semi-rigid heel counter and wraparound overlays, with generally good lateral lockdown from the upper.
Durability: PUMAGRIP outsole showed very strong grip and minimal early wear (no visible denting reported), and overall durability expectation was rated good.

Cushioning: Updated dual-layer PEBA setup (38/30 mm) feels softer and bouncier than v3 while staying controlled; impact protection is described as soft-yet-firm, with the heel as the softest landing zone and a balanced forefoot feel.
Responsiveness: The ride is more energetic and dynamic, with improved bounce/energy return from the new foams; the revised PWRPLATE provides a long, snappy flex and smoother, quicker toe-off.
Stability: A wider midfoot platform (+8 mm) helps the base, but support is less locked-in than v3; reviewers note reduced arch/midfoot guidance and want more heel-counter/ankle-collar support.
Durability: Long-term durability evidence is limited in this excerpt; no explicit outsole wear or material longevity results are provided, beyond short-term comfort over runs up to about 15 miles.

Cushioning: The dual-density setup (softer PEBA-based top layer over a firmer Nitrofoam layer) makes v4 softer than prior versions but still more "racy" than plush, with better impact give at landing and toe-off plus a smoother heel-to-forefoot transition from the 38/30 mm stack and 8 mm drop.

Responsiveness: The ride stays energetic and quick, with strong snappiness/energy return from the plated construction (PWRPlate/carbon-composite plate) and firmer lower foam that preserves the Deviate’s signature responsive feel.

Stability: Heel and collar structure provide secure lockdown, and reviewers noted reliable ankle hold despite being a plated shoe; the slightly wider fit and firmer plated platform improve overall lateral confidence and torsional control.

Durability: PUMAGRIP remains a standout for sticky traction, especially in wet conditions; although rubber is thinner with more cutouts for weight reduction, early testing did not show obvious durability loss.

specsDecision: No automatic score/spec change proposed. Conflicts were recorded for reviewer decision.
